about: manut's one masker for token-like text: the desktop shell (tasks.rs mask_secrets, mask_command) and the page (src/lib/secrets.ts maskSecrets, maskCommand) use these patterns, and secrets.cases.json holds the table both run (`cases` for text, `command` for what an approval shows). Two forms. maskSecrets is for text that never runs (a chat, a diff, a skill's files, a title run's material); maskCommand is for anything an approval shows (the command, a tool's arguments, the folder), on the card, the phone, Home, Needs you and a notification. maskSecrets: `whole` goes first, each [pattern, flags, kind] replaced whole by `mask` (a private key block from its BEGIN line to its END line, or to the end of the base64 lines after it when there is no END, whose body never holds a character the shell acts on; provider-prefixed tokens and JSON web tokens, kind `word`: only as a whole word). `split` next: a family with a fixed body length (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_: 36 of [A-Za-z0-9]; glpat-: 20 of [A-Za-z0-9_-]) broken by up to four line breaks or single spaces, in any letter case. Each entry is [pattern, length]; group 1 is the body's pieces, which are counted in order, and when they make exactly `length` characters at the end of a piece the prefix and those pieces are replaced by `mask` (the pieces after stay). Otherwise the text is left for `tokens`. `tokens` (its `{prefixes}`) is replaced whole by `mask`; it also takes a token broken by line breaks or a space (up to four breaks), joining a next piece only when that piece is token-shaped (two or more capitals or digits), so a prose word after the break stays. A `tokens` match is a key only when it stands alone (no `edge` character glued to either side) and has a key's shape: it has a provider's `exact` shape and length, or after its prefix it holds a capital or a digit (`needs`), and a `wordlike` prefix (`sk-`, which CSS classes, locales and names also start with) needs one of the `named` forms or a `run` of 16 letters and digits holding a capital or a digit, so `rm -rf sk-releases-backup` stays as it is. `names` is the set of secret names that `{names}` stands for in `kept` and `assigned` (since item 117 also `pass` and `pwd` as a name's own part, `DB_PASS`, `MYSQL_PWD`, but not `bypass` or `PWD`, `APP_KEY` and `SECRET_KEY_BASE`). `kept` goes after `tokens`: each [pattern, flags] has three groups, the first and third kept and the second replaced by `mask` (a quoted value after a secret name and `:` or `=`; a YAML line whose value is one word to the line's end, so prose after a colon stays; credentials in HTTP headers, a lone Bearer and a Cookie; the password of `scheme://user:pass@host`; `--password value` on a command line; since item 117 also a name with blanks round `=` whose one-word value runs to the line's end and holds a digit, `/`, `+` or `=` or is 16 long, as `~/.aws/credentials` writes it; a vendor's `_KEY=` on an environment line; a JSON `"key"`; `.netrc`'s login and password; `curl -u` and `mysql -p`; Slack's and Discord's webhook addresses, which keep their host). `assigned` (case-insensitive) keeps its name and `=` and replaces the value. A `kept` or `assigned` value is no key when it is a reference (`ref`: it starts with a backtick or `$`, as `${DB_PASSWORD}` or `` `Bearer ${token}` `` do) or a word that says there is none (`plain`, in any case: none, null, nil, true, false, undefined, `~`) (item 117). maskCommand (item 117, item 121) first masks each private key block (`blocks`: from its BEGIN line through its END line, a block with no END (none before the next BEGIN, `blockEnd`, `blockBegin`) up to its last base64 line, and the one-line form with `\\n` between its lines) when every line of its body is base64 or a PEM header (`Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED`, `DEK-Info: AES-128-CBC,0A1B`): its BEGIN and END lines stay shown and its body becomes one `mask` line. Only where the whole block is data the shell hands a writer: inside a quoted string or a heredoc's body that belongs to the command's first simple command, whose first word is one of `sinks` (they only write their input out), in a command with no `|`, `(` or `)`, read as secrets.ts `lex` reads it (it follows `$'...'`, `<<<`, a heredoc's whole terminator word, a comment only where a word starts, and nothing from a substitution or arithmetic on, nor in an unquoted heredoc's body from its first `$(`, `${`, backtick or backslash). A block anywhere else, or whose body holds anything else, is not masked at all, and the `whole` entry of kind `block` is not used on a command. Then it reads a command as the shell will: line by line, so no masked value spans a line break; nothing is joined across a blank or a line (`split` is not used, and `word` stands for `tokens`); and a masked value stops at the first character in `shell` (a blank of any kind, either quote, `#`, `*`, `?`, `[`, `]`, a backtick, `$`, `(`, `)`, `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `{`, `}`, a backslash, a line break), which is shown with everything after it, so a value that starts with one is not masked at all. Last, the structural check: the masked command must split into exactly the command's shell words, each the same or with only a run of characters outside `shell` masked (a key block's, data as above), and the command must not already hold the mask's character; otherwise it is shown as it is, marked `unmasked`, and every surface says it may hold a key. A key a command holds is still masked; a substitution, a pipe, a second command or a command's own operand never is. Flags are JavaScript's (`i`, `m`); the shell builds the same with RegexBuilder, and reads `\b` as an ASCII word boundary, as JavaScript does, so a token right after Thai text is masked by both. `hidden` (item 121) lists, as ranges of code points, the characters that do not show or that reorder what does: control characters but a tab, a line break and a carriage return; the soft hyphen; the combining grapheme joiner; the Arabic letter mark; Hangul fillers; Khmer's and Mongolian's invisible signs; the zero-width spaces and joiners and the direction marks (U+200B to U+200F); the line and paragraph separators and the direction embeddings and overrides (U+2028 to U+202E); the word joiner, invisible operators and direction isolates (U+2060 to U+206F); variation selectors; the byte order mark; the interlinear annotation characters; shorthand and musical format controls; and the tag characters. In the command form, and in every text an ask shows (`revealHidden`), each one is replaced by `hiddenMark` with its code point in capital hex, at least four digits, and the card says the command holds hidden characters; a masked value stops at one, so it is shown.
